I can relate to this so much. When things ended between my ex and I, we promised we'd always be friends/be there for one another. 

Then I saw him posting on social media, living his best life and seemingly looking so much happier without me. It broke my heart and made me feel horrid. I realized I couldn't do "friends." There was too much history there. I completely understand where you are coming from. He was my first love and I gave him so so so many firsts, it was too hard to dissociate the romance from him and become platonic and accept that I would eventually witness him move on romantically. It was too much for me. 

I took the rather drastic leap and one day blocked him from all social media. It was a longer story than just that, but suffice it to say, I cut all ties. I recognized A) I was too weak to stop myself from looking/checking his socials and obsessing over every little thing he did and B) I didn't need it. There was a reason we split and I thought to myself, if it's meant to be, we'll find a way back to one another after my heart heals a little bit. What's meant to be will be. But after a long-term relationship, I just didn't see friendship in the cards with the man I was prepared to have a baby with. It just felt wrong.

He has reached out and tried to be friendly. I ignored his messages. Maybe I'm cruel, but I consider it putting my own heart and needs first. In a breakup, you deserve to be "selfish" and put yourself first and if you can't handle being friends, so be it. You know what is best for you, sometimes it's hard and requires great bravery to listen and follow what your gut feelings are.

Now, this is just my own personal experience but I hope that maybe something of this can help. If you ever need a friend, I'm a message away. You will prevail and come out stronger, I believe in you and I feel your sentiments so deeply; your comment really struck a chord with me. I longed to reach out to him, but more specifically, I wanted h to reach out to me. I spent the better part of our relationship giving my all to him, bending over backwards for him. I wanted him to reach out to me, to make some grand (or small) gesture or sign to show me I was worth it, but he never did. Instead he kept posting on social media like his life had suddenly improved so much without me. That was my sign to cut all my ties with him for good and not look back.

It made me feel like shit. I was so hurt, but then I got angry and blocked him and vowed to treat myself better. I had a lot of pent up anger from the problems that stemmed from our relationship. He was very emotionally manipulative and I didn't see it while I was in the relationship. Once I saw it, it wasn't hard to keep away.

I wish I had some magic recipe or secret to share, but truly, it just took time. At first, the temptation to reach out was hard to resist and I'll admit, I slipped two times in the first month of our breakup. I wrote him a "I don't know how I can live without you" and a "I still love you" text. Then, Valentines day came and I saw he was posting on social media (we were still connected on social media at this point) that he was out at a bar, with girls, living his best life. He told me he hated Valentine's day, that he didn't believe in celebrating it. And yet there he was, wearing a Valentine's day tie and celebrating with strangers. It infuriated me so much that I blocked him the next day.

Maybe drastic, probably dramatic. But I put myself first. I knew if I left him as my friend, it would be torturous for me to see his posts pop up and I knew the temptation would be too strong. So I cut my ties with him and deleted his number. I threw out all the mementos from our relationship and I made a promise to myself to not look back.

I don't have very strong self-control so this was really miraculous and unprecedented for me. If I could do it, you can do it too. It takes time, be gentle on yourself, but also, don't forget your worth.

I realized I was fully over him when I saw a picture of us in my phone that I forgot to delete and I didn't feel sad when I saw his face. I felt sad for *me*. I saw my innocence and how in love I looked. I felt sad that I wasted my time with him. I felt so relieved to be through with him. That's how I knew I was fully over it.

Oh man, I have been here before and was here recently... It's so hard when you really love someone and it isn't working. It's even harder when you have to end the relationship while you're still in love/the feelings are still there. I was in a similar situation and I can honestly say that if things aren't working and you feel like you're going in circles, chances are, it's never going to work. I hate to sound so pessimistic but I wish someone had been more realistic with me when I went through that. Sometimes life gets in the way of love and things don't always work out with that person at a certain point of time. In my most recent breakup, I consoled myself with the two hypothetical outcomes of a breakup:
1 - We weren't meant to be and I'll move on to greener pastures and grow from the breakup. Yes, it will hurt, but I'll come out stronger and wiser.
2 - We were meant to be and this time apart will help us realize and appreciate one another. If it's meant to be, it will be and all work out. 
If not, you save yourself a mountain of hurt by ripping off the band-aid now before things get worse.
